what: Apnimed is a late-stage drug company developing Oxnimbi, an oral pill to treat obstructive sleep apnea.
proceeds: It expects net proceeds of about $173.6 million. With its existing cash, about $237.8 million will go to getting Oxnimbi approved and, if approved, launching it. The rest will fund research on other drug candidates, working capital and general costs.
risks: The company has lost a lot of money since it started, expects more losses, and may never become profitable.
The pro forma financial figures rest on early estimates and assumptions, so real results could be very different.
Its current and future debt could make it harder to run the business.
Even after this offering, it will need much more money, and may have to delay or cut programs if it cannot raise it.
